Synopsis:
US-Iran military exchanges have resumed, driving Brent crude above $95 and pushing the US 10-year Treasury yield to a 3-year intraday high of 4.8122%. The dual shock of geopolitical risk and an oil-driven inflation resurgence is pressuring global bond markets. Japan's BOJ signals continued rate hikes, threatening to redirect Japanese capital away from overseas bonds. Equity markets are broadly selling off across Asia and Europe. Fixed income is under multi-front assault: fiscal deficits, oil inflation, and rising Japanese yields reducing a key pillar of global bond demand.
